title: Assessing the Breathless Patient as a PCP
next: Chapter 29, Lesson 2: Asthma, COPD, the upper airway and the PCP's bronchospasm drugs

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already sit breathless patients up, give oxygen, count breaths and bag when breathing fails. Today, as a PCP:

  1. Tell an airway problem from a breathing problem
  2. Judge how sick from position, effort, mind and skin
  3. Focused history, exam and auscultation that guide treatment

Textbook: Chapter 29, PDF pages 2404–2466
slides.say: Welcome to Chapter twenty-nine, respiratory emergencies. Shortness of breath, or dyspnea, is one of the most common reasons people call us. As EMRs you already know the basics: sit the patient up, give oxygen, count the breaths, and bag them when breathing fails. As a PCP, you now carry drugs and pressure tools, and the decision to use them rests on your assessment. Today we'll cover three things: airway problems versus breathing problems, how to judge how sick a breathless patient is, and a focused history, exam and chest assessment that points you to the right treatment.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎来到第二十九章，呼吸系统急症。气短，也就是呼吸困难，是人们叫救护车最常见的原因之一。作为 EMR，基本功你们都会：扶病人坐起、给氧、数呼吸、呼吸衰竭时用球囊面罩通气。作为 PCP，你现在手里有药物和正压工具，用不用全靠你的评估。今天讲三件事：气道问题和呼吸问题的区别；怎么判断一个气短的病人有多重；怎么做有针对性的问诊、查体和胸部评估，把你引向正确的处置。

slides.title: Airway problem or breathing problem?
slides.body:
An open airway is not enough breathing

  • Airway: snoring, gurgling, stridor → position, suction, adjuncts
  • 4 levels: airways, alveoli, nerve–muscle, chest wall
  • Hard to breathe out → obstructive disease (asthma, COPD)
  • Hard to breathe in → upper airway obstruction
  • Oxygen can hold SpO₂ up while CO₂ keeps climbing
slides.say: First, separate the airway from breathing. An airway problem is about the open tube: snoring, gurgling, stridor. You fix it with positioning, suction and adjuncts, and you keep rechecking. But an open airway doesn't mean enough air is moving. Breathing problems sit at four levels: the airways, like asthma; the alveoli, like pneumonia; the nerves and muscles, like a high spinal cord injury; or the chest wall, like a flail chest. A quick clue: trouble breathing out suggests asthma or COPD; trouble breathing in suggests the upper airway. And oxygen can keep the saturation normal while carbon dioxide keeps rising.
slides.sayZh: 先把气道和呼吸分开。气道问题关乎这根管子通不通：打鼾声、咕噜声、喘鸣。靠摆体位、吸引和气道辅助装置解决，并且要反复复查。但气道通畅不等于换气足够。呼吸问题分四个层面：气道，比如哮喘；肺泡，比如肺炎；神经和肌肉，比如高位脊髓损伤；胸廓，比如连枷胸。一个快速线索：呼气费劲提示哮喘或 COPD；吸气费劲提示上气道问题。还要记住，给氧可以让血氧读数保持正常，而二氧化碳却在继续升高。

slides.title: The whole body in a breathing call
slides.body:
SystemWhat to look for
Brainanxiety early; confusion, lethargy, coma late
Heartmild hypoxia → fast HR; severe → slow HR, VF/VT
Musclestiring: slower, shallower, sleepy = failing
Kidneysfluid and acid problems that look like lung disease
slides.say: A good respiratory assessment looks beyond the lungs. The brain is very sensitive to low oxygen: anxiety is an early sign, while confusion, lethargy and coma come late. Mild hypoxia speeds the heart up, but severe hypoxia often slows it, and uncorrected hypoxia can trigger ventricular fibrillation or ventricular tachycardia. The breathing muscles can only work hard for so long. An asthmatic may compensate for hours, then tire, get sleepy, and breathe slower and shallower. That's respiratory failure, not improvement. And sick kidneys can put acid in the blood and cause fast breathing that looks like a lung problem.
slides.sayZh: 好的呼吸评估要跳出肺来看。大脑对缺氧非常敏感：焦虑是早期征象，意识混乱、嗜睡、昏迷出现得晚。轻度缺氧心跳加快，重度缺氧常常心跳变慢，缺氧不纠正可诱发室颤或室速。呼吸肌只能拼命工作一段时间：哮喘病人可以代偿好几个小时，然后累了、犯困，呼吸变慢变浅。那是呼吸衰竭，不是好转。肾脏有病会让血液里有酸，引起呼吸快，看起来像肺的问题。

slides.title: First look: position tells a story
slides.body:
• Tripod: leaning forward on hands or knees, working hard
  • Sniffing position: trying to open the upper airway
  • Head bobbing: exhausted, often pre-terminal
  • Breathless but willing to lie flat: may be crashing
  • Full sentences = mild; 2–3 words, bolt upright = severe

Body-type clues (barrel chest, tall and thin, smoker on the pill) are only clues: confirm them.
slides.say: Your first look tells you a lot. The tripod position, leaning forward on the hands or knees, steadies the shoulders so the extra breathing muscles work better. A head tilted back in the sniffing position is trying to open the upper airway. When that patient tires, the head lifts on each breath in and drops on the breath out. That's head bobbing, and it often comes just before collapse. Be very worried by a breathless patient who is willing to lie flat. Full sentences mean mild distress; sitting bolt upright, managing two or three words, may mean life-threatening distress.
slides.sayZh: 第一眼就能看出很多。三脚架位，就是身体前倾、双手撑在膝盖或桌上，能稳住肩膀，让辅助呼吸肌更好用力。头后仰呈嗅物位，是在拼命打开上气道。这样的病人累了以后，吸气时抬头、呼气时垂头，这叫点头呼吸，常出现在垮掉之前。气短却愿意平躺的病人要高度警惕。能说完整句子是轻度窘迫；笔直端坐、只能说两三个词，可能已危及生命。

slides.title: Work of breathing: see and hear
slides.body:
Seeretractions, nasal flaring, tracheal tuggingsee-saw breathing
Hearsnoring, gurgling, stridornoisy = obstructed
Countrate × depthdepth is misjudged most

Fast but quiet, with clear lungs? Think acidosis, sepsis or shock. A bronchodilator won't help.
slides.say: Next, the work of breathing. Look for retractions above the collarbones, between the ribs and below the sternum; nasal flaring; tracheal tugging; and see-saw movement of the chest and belly. Any noise you can hear from the doorway is abnormal: snoring is the tongue, gurgling is fluid, and stridor, a harsh high sound on breathing in, is usually a swollen larynx. Count the rate, and judge the depth, which is the part we misjudge most. And watch for quiet tachypnea: fast breathing with clear lungs. Think acidosis, sepsis or shock. A nebulized bronchodilator won't help any of those.
slides.sayZh: 接着看呼吸做功。看锁骨上、肋间、胸骨下有没有凹陷；鼻翼扇动；气管牵曳；胸腹跷跷板样反向运动。在门口就能听到的声音都不正常：打鼾是舌头，咕噜声是液体，喘鸣是吸气时粗糙高调的声音，通常是喉头肿了。数频率，也要判断深度，深度是最容易看错的。还要警惕「安静的呼吸急促」：呼吸快但肺音清晰。想到酸中毒、脓毒症或休克，雾化支气管扩张剂对这些都没用。

slides.q: Your asthma patient has had two salbutamol treatments. The wheezes are softer, but she is drowsy and her rate has dropped from 34 to 14. What does this most likely mean?
options: She is improving; the salbutamol is working
She is tiring out and moving very little air
The oximeter probe has slipped off
slides.say: Let's pause for a question. Your asthma patient has had two salbutamol treatments. The wheezes are softer, but she's drowsy, and her breathing rate has dropped from thirty-four to fourteen. What does this most likely mean? A, she is improving; the salbutamol is working. B, she is tiring out and moving very little air. C, she is hyperventilating from anxiety. D, the oximeter probe has slipped off. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 停一下考考你。你的哮喘病人已经用了两次沙丁胺醇，哮鸣音变轻了，但她开始犯困，呼吸频率从三十四降到十四。这最可能说明什么？A 她在好转，沙丁胺醇起效了；B 她累垮了，几乎没在换气；C 她因焦虑在过度通气；D 血氧探头掉了。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. Softer wheezes with drowsiness and a falling rate mean fatigue and rising carbon dioxide, not recovery. A wheeze needs moving air, so a quiet chest can mean almost no air is moving. Get ready to assist her breathing with a BVM. A is the dangerous assumption: real improvement looks more alert and talks more easily. C doesn't fit a drowsy patient who is slowing down, and D can't explain the change in her mental status.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。哮鸣音变轻，同时犯困、频率下降，说明的是疲劳和二氧化碳升高，不是康复。哮鸣音要有气流才能产生，胸部变安静可能意味着几乎没有气体进出。要准备用球囊面罩辅助通气。A 是最危险的误判：真正的好转是病人更清醒、说话更轻松。C 不符合一个昏昏欲睡、呼吸变慢的病人，D 解释不了她神志的变化。

slides.title: Mind and skin: the brain's blood gas
slides.body:
FindingPoints to
Restless, confused, combativelow oxygen
Sleepy, hard to rousehigh CO₂
Cyanosislate: about SpO₂ 65% at normal Hb
Chocolate brownmethemoglobin (nitrates, toxins)
Cherry redcarbon monoxide (late sign)

Check the mouth, under the eyelids and the nail beds.
slides.say: You can't measure blood gases on scene, but the patient's brain does it for you. Low oxygen makes people restless, confused, even combative. High carbon dioxide sedates them, so they become sleepy and hard to rouse. Cyanosis comes late: with normal hemoglobin, a person turns blue only when about fifty grams per litre of it carries no oxygen. That's a saturation of roughly sixty-five percent! An anemic patient may never look blue. Chocolate-brown membranes suggest methemoglobin, from nitrates or toxins; cherry-red skin is a late sign of carbon monoxide. Check inside the mouth, under the eyelids and the nail beds.
slides.sayZh: 现场测不了血气，但病人的大脑一直在替你测。缺氧让人烦躁、意识混乱，甚至有攻击性。二氧化碳高有镇静作用，病人会嗜睡、难唤醒。发绀出现得晚：血红蛋白正常的人，要大约每升五十克血红蛋白没带氧才会发紫，相当于血氧约百分之六十五！贫血的病人可能根本不发紫。黏膜呈巧克力褐色提示高铁血红蛋白，来自硝酸盐或毒物；樱桃红色皮肤是一氧化碳中毒的晚期征象。要看口腔里面、下眼睑内侧和甲床。

slides.title: The focused history
slides.body:
• Can't talk? Ask yes/no questions; use family and medications
  • Sudden onset: bronchospasm, anaphylaxis, PE, pneumothorax
  • Waking at night breathless (PND): left heart failure or COPD
  • "Ever intubated for this?" "Better or worse than last time?"
  • What have you already taken, and did it help?
  • Look beyond the lungs: heart attack, kidneys, diabetes
slides.say: Now the history. A breathless patient may manage only a few words, so ask yes-or-no questions, use the family, and read the medication bottles. Often you start treatment first and finish the story later. Sudden onset suggests bronchospasm, anaphylaxis, a pulmonary embolism or a pneumothorax. Paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, waking suddenly at night short of breath, is an ominous sign of left heart failure, worsening COPD, or both. Ask: have you ever been intubated for this? Is it better or worse than last time? What have you taken, and did it help? And look beyond the lungs: a heart attack can present as heart failure.
slides.sayZh: 再说问诊。气短的病人可能只能说几个词，所以改问是非题，问家属，看药瓶。很多时候先处置、病史之后再补。突然起病提示支气管痉挛、过敏性休克、肺栓塞或气胸。夜间阵发性呼吸困难，也就是夜里突然憋醒，是左心衰、COPD 加重或两者兼有的凶兆。要问：以前因为这个插过管吗？比上次好还是差？用过什么药，有没有用？还要跳出肺来看：心梗也可能表现为心衰。

slides.title: Neck, chest and legs
slides.body:
• JVD sitting up: high pressure on the right side of the heart
  • JVD + low BP in trauma: tamponade or tension pneumothorax
  • Press the liver, neck veins fill more: right heart failure
  • Tracheal deviation: classic, but late and rare
  • Legs and hands: pitting edema, clubbing, fever or clammy skin
slides.say: Your physical exam now goes deeper. Look at the neck veins with the patient semi-sitting. Jugular venous distention, or JVD, while sitting up suggests high pressure on the right side of the heart, from heart failure or from high pressure in the chest. In a trauma patient with a pressure of eighty over forty, distended neck veins should make you think of cardiac tamponade or a tension pneumothorax. Press gently on the liver: if the neck veins fill even more, that's hepatojugular reflux, a specific sign of right heart failure. Tracheal deviation is classic, but late and rare. Then check for pitting edema and finger clubbing.
slides.sayZh: 现在查体要更深入。病人半坐位时看颈静脉。坐着还颈静脉怒张，提示右心压力高，来自心衰或胸腔内压力高。创伤病人血压八十比四十却颈静脉怒张，要想到心包填塞或张力性气胸。轻压肝脏，颈静脉更鼓了，这叫肝颈静脉回流征，是右心衰的特异体征。气管偏移很经典，但出现晚、也少见。然后查凹陷性水肿和杵状指。

slides.title: Listening: where to put the stethoscope
slides.body:
• Right lung 3 lobes, left lung 2: not symmetrical
  • Pneumonia and heart failure settle in the bases: listen on the back
  • Right middle lobe: below or beside the right breast
  • Air-filled chest (asthma, COPD): sounds distant or absent
  • Wet or solid lung (pneumonia, CHF): sounds louder
slides.say: Auscultation is where a PCP earns their treatment decisions. The lungs aren't symmetrical: the right has three lobes, the left only two. Pneumonia and heart failure settle in the bases with gravity, and the bases are heard almost only from the back. The upper lobes are in front; the right middle lobe is below or beside the right breast. One useful piece of physics: sound travels better through fluid than through air. So a chest full of trapped air, as in asthma or COPD, sounds distant or silent, while a wet or solid lung, as in pneumonia or heart failure, sounds louder than you expect.
slides.sayZh: 听诊是 PCP 做治疗决定的依据。两肺不对称：右肺三叶，左肺只有两叶。肺炎和心衰会随重力沉到肺底，而肺底几乎只能从背部听到。上叶在前胸，右中叶在右乳下方或外侧。一条有用的物理规律：声音在液体里比在空气里传得好。所以胸腔里困满气体时，比如哮喘或 COPD，呼吸音遥远甚至听不到；而湿的或实变的肺，比如肺炎或心衰，听起来比预想的响。

slides.title: What the added sounds mean
slides.body:
SoundThink of
Wheeze: high, whistlingnarrow airways (asthma, CHF); one side: foreign body
Crackles: pops, clicksfluid (CHF, pneumonia)
Rhonchi: low, rattlingthick secretions in big airways
Nothingno air moving: danger

Wheeze gone after a bronchodilator = muscle spasm. Still there = maybe inflammation.
slides.say: Now the added sounds. Wheezes are high whistles from air squeezing through narrow airways, usually everywhere in asthma, and also in heart failure. Asthma rarely wheezes on one side only, so a one-sided wheeze may be a foreign body or secretions; have the patient cough and listen again. Crackles are pops and clicks that usually mean fluid. Rhonchi are low rattles from thick secretions. And here's a link to your drugs: smooth muscle only surrounds the larger airways. A wheeze that clears after a bronchodilator was spasm; one that stays may be inflammation. The worst sound is no sound. Silence means danger.
slides.sayZh: 再看附加音。哮鸣音是气流挤过狭窄气道发出的高调哨音，哮喘时通常遍布两肺，心衰时也有。哮喘很少只在一侧有哮鸣，所以单侧哮鸣可能是异物或分泌物，让病人咳一下再听。湿啰音是噼啪声，通常意味着有液体。干啰音是稠痰造成的低调呼噜声。这里和你的药物有关：平滑肌只包绕较大的气道。用了支气管扩张剂后消失的哮鸣音是痉挛；不消失的可能是炎症。最危险的是没有声音：寂静意味着危险。

slides.title: EMR vs PCP: the respiratory assessment
slides.body:
BC SOB (asthma/COPD) protocol and BC assessment model

All licence levels (EMR + PCP)

  • Primary survey; O₂ to SpO₂ ≥ 94%
  • Position of comfort, usually sitting forward
  • Auscultation
  • History and a baseline set of vital signs

PCP adds

  • Functional enquiry: 9 body systems
  • Includes respiratory and cardiovascular
  • Skipping a system: 5% off (max 15% in total)
  • Findings guide ipratropium, epinephrine, dexamethasone, CPAP
slides.say: Here's how the assessment splits in BC. The left column, from the BC protocol for shortness of breath with asthma or COPD, is familiar: a primary survey, oxygen aiming for ninety-four percent, a position of comfort, auscultation, a history and a baseline set of vital signs. The right column is new. In the BC assessment model, the PCP adds a functional enquiry: a quick review of nine body systems, including respiratory and cardiovascular. In the practical exam, a system you don't ask about costs five percent, up to fifteen percent in total. And your findings now decide whether you add ipratropium, epinephrine, dexamethasone or CPAP.
slides.sayZh: BC 的评估是这样分工的。左栏来自 BC「哮喘/COPD 气短」流程，都很熟悉：初步评估、给氧使血氧达到百分之九十四、舒适体位、听诊、问病史、测一组基线生命体征。右栏是新的：在 BC 评估模型里，PCP 要加做系统问诊（functional enquiry），快速过一遍九个身体系统，包括呼吸和心血管。实操考试中，漏问一个系统扣百分之五，整个系统问诊最多扣百分之十五。而且现在由你的发现决定要不要加异丙托溴铵、肾上腺素、地塞米松或 CPAP。

slides.q: A 30-year-old breathes 32 times a minute. Lungs are clear at all six points, SpO₂ 98% on room air, and his breath smells fruity. Your EMR partner suggests salbutamol. Best response?
options: Give salbutamol 5 mg by nebulizer to be safe
Have him breathe into a paper bag
Suspect a metabolic cause such as DKA: check glucose, support, transport
slides.say: Let's try a PCP decision. A thirty-year-old is breathing thirty-two times a minute. His lungs are clear at all six points, his saturation is ninety-eight percent on room air, and his breath smells fruity. Your EMR partner suggests salbutamol. What's the best response? A, give salbutamol five milligrams by nebulizer to be safe. B, have him breathe into a paper bag. C, suspect a metabolic cause such as diabetic ketoacidosis: check his glucose, support him, and transport. D, start CPAP at five centimetres of water. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来一道 PCP 决策题。一位三十岁男性每分钟呼吸三十二次，六个点听诊肺音都清晰，不吸氧血氧百分之九十八，呼气有烂水果味。你的 EMR 搭档建议给沙丁胺醇。最好的回应是什么？A 保险起见雾化五毫克沙丁胺醇；B 让他对着纸袋呼吸；C 怀疑代谢原因，比如糖尿病酮症酸中毒：测血糖、支持治疗、转运；D 以五厘米水柱启动 CPAP。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is C. Fast breathing with clear lungs, a normal saturation and a fruity odour points to diabetic ketoacidosis: the body is breathing off acid. Check the glucose and treat what you find. A won't help, because bronchodilators only treat bronchospasm, and there's none here. B is dangerous; rebreathing works against his compensation and can lower his oxygen. D is wrong because BC's CPAP needs a saturation under ninety-four percent on oxygen, plus other signs of distress.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 C。呼吸快、肺音清、血氧正常、呼气有水果味，指向糖尿病酮症酸中毒：身体在靠呼吸排酸。测血糖，按结果处理。A 没用，因为支气管扩张剂只治支气管痉挛，而这里没有痉挛。B 很危险：回吸气体会破坏他的代偿，还可能让他缺氧。D 错在 BC 的 CPAP 要求吸氧状态下血氧仍低于百分之九十四，并伴其他窘迫征象。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• Not every fast breather needs a bronchodilator: pain, DKA, sepsis
  • Softer wheezes + sleepy patient = failing, not better
  • SpO₂ can't see carbon monoxide: the number may look normal
  • The sicker they are, the faster SpO₂ falls (steep curve)
  • After every treatment: breath sounds + SpO₂ again, and record it
slides.say: Now the traps that matter more now that you carry drugs. First, not every fast breather needs a bronchodilator; the book warns that nebulizing patients whose fast breathing comes from pain, anxiety, ketoacidosis or sepsis doesn't help. Second, softer wheezes in a sleepy patient mean failure, not success. Third, a normal oximeter reading can hide carbon monoxide, because the device can't tell the two apart. Fourth, the oxygen curve is steep at the bottom, so the more hypoxic the patient, the faster the saturation falls. Fifth, after every treatment, listen again, recheck the saturation, and record the change, as the BC oxygen protocol asks.
slides.sayZh: 现在你手里有药了，这些陷阱更要注意。第一，不是每个呼吸快的人都需要支气管扩张剂；书里提醒，给疼痛、焦虑、酮症酸中毒或脓毒症引起呼吸快的病人做雾化，没用。第二，病人犯困时哮鸣音变轻，是衰竭，不是成功。第三，脉氧读数正常也可能掩盖一氧化碳中毒，因为仪器分不清两者。第四，氧解离曲线在低端很陡，病人越缺氧，血氧掉得越快。第五，每次治疗后都要重新听诊、复查血氧并记录变化，这是 BC 给氧流程的要求。

slides.title: For the BC exam
slides.body:
• Book: OPQRST. BC scoring: OPQRRRST and LOTARP
  • Book: compare sides, bases from the back. BC: 6 points front or back
  • Book: SpO₂ over 95% is normal. BC target: ≥ 94%
  • Asthma/COPD: BC warns 94% may not be achievable
  • PCP only: functional enquiry, 9 systems, max 15% off

The book's peak flow cut-offs (< 300 moderate, < 200 L/min severe) aren't in the BC protocols.
slides.say: A few BC points for the exam. The textbook uses OPQRST; BC scoring uses OPQRRRST and LOTARP. The book says to compare sides and listen to the bases from the back; BC expects at least six points on the front or six on the back. The book calls a saturation above ninety-five percent normal; your BC target is ninety-four percent or higher, and for asthma or COPD the protocol warns it may not be achievable. The functional enquiry is PCP-only. And the book's peak flow cut-offs, under three hundred litres a minute for a moderate attack and under two hundred for a severe one, aren't in the BC protocols.
slides.sayZh: 几个 BC 考点。教材用 OPQRST；BC 评分用 OPQRRRST 和 LOTARP。书里说左右对比、肺底从背部听；BC 要求至少前胸六个点或后背六个点。书里说血氧高于百分之九十五算正常；BC 目标是百分之九十四或以上，而哮喘或 COPD 流程提醒这可能达不到。系统问诊是 PCP 独有的。书里的呼气峰流速分界，低于每分钟三百升算中度发作、低于两百算重度，不在 BC 流程里。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. Open airway ≠ enough breathing: watch for tiring and a quiet chest
  2. Position, words per breath, mind and skin tell you how sick
  3. Listen at 6 points, know each sound, reassess after every treatment

Next: asthma, COPD, the upper airway, and the PCP's bronchospasm drugs
slides.say: Three things to remember. One: an open airway isn't the same as enough breathing. Watch for the tired patient: head bobbing, a slowing rate, drowsiness and a quiet chest. Two: position, words per breath, mental status and skin tell you how sick the patient is before any monitor does. Three: listen at least six points, know what each sound means, and reassess after every treatment. Next lesson: the upper airway, asthma and COPD, and the PCP's bronchospasm drugs, ipratropium, dexamethasone and intramuscular epinephrine, with their BC doses. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 收尾三句话。一，气道通畅不等于呼吸够。警惕累垮的病人：点头呼吸、频率变慢、犯困、胸部变安静。二，体位、一口气能说几个词、神志和皮肤，比任何监护仪都更早告诉你病人有多重。三，至少听六个点，弄懂每种声音的含义，每次治疗后都要复评。下节课讲上气道、哮喘和 COPD，以及 PCP 治疗支气管痉挛的药物：异丙托溴铵、地塞米松和肌注肾上腺素，还有它们的 BC 剂量。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
